title: Client resilience playbook: unified timeout windows, idempotency envelope, and hedged-call semantics
creator: Evan Liu
description: Problem: Services and client SDKs at Redwood have grown divergent retry/timeout semantics. This causes inconsistent failure modes during multi-region failover, edge cases with non-idempotent requests, and skewed SLO observability. Goal: define a cross-service 'client resilience playbook' that standardizes timeout windows, backoff envelopes, idempotency envelope construction, hedged-request semantics, and circuit-breaker-load-shedding interactions so application teams and SDKs behave predictably under load and during failovers.
acceptance_criteria:
1) A concise spec document published in Confluence that describes: canonical timeout + hedging windows for low/med/high latency SLOs, idempotency envelope format and propagation rules, client-side hedged request algorithm, and circuit breaker integration points.
2) SDK changes (JS + Go + Python) submitted as PRs implementing defaults from the spec and unit tests validating idempotency propagation and single-effect guarantee for non-idempotent endpoints.
3) Runtime integration PR that exposes request metadata (idempotency key, hedged=true/false, chosen-attempt) to per-route observability so rollout and incident debugging is possible.
4) A two-week canary showing reduced tail-latency spike incidents during simulated regional capacity loss (internal chaos test).
decisions:
- Adopt dual-window timeouts: 'dispatch' window (client attempts + hedges) and 'service' deadline propagated via x-redwood-deadline-ms header.
- Default hedging enabled for idempotent read-like endpoints only; non-idempotent write endpoints require explicit opt-in via @idempotent annotation in server API registry.
- Idempotency envelope: use UUIDv4 + origin metadata (sdk, region, timestamp) encoded in base64; envelope carried as x-redwood-idempotency header and logged by runtime.
- Backoff: use a capped jittered exponential backoff with base=50ms, cap=2s for client retries; hedged attempt scheduled at 60% of dispatch window.
- Circuit breaker: client observes per-route 5xx rate and OPEN state; when circuit is OPEN, client applies deterministic local backoff and drops hedged attempts to avoid amplification.
- Security: idempotency header contains no PII; older servers ignore unknown headers gracefully.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (spec & SDK): Draft spec -> internal review (eng + PM + platform security) -> SDK implementation for JS + Go + Python implementing header format, default retry/hedge timers, and idempotency envelope generation.
Phase 2 (runtime & observability): Add support in runtime to ingest x-redwood-idempotency and x-redwood-deadline-ms into trace/span attributes; expose new dashboard widgets for hedged vs single-attempt outcomes and idempotency collisions.
Phase 3 (canary & rollout): Canary on non-critical routes, run chaos test (region-terminate) and monitor tail latency + error rates, then progressively roll out to higher-traffic routes.
References: Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RES/Client+Resilience+Playbook (internal), SDK PR (JS): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/820 (WIP), Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/12345 (linked).
rollout_plan:
- Week 1: Spec reviewed and approved by Resilience Working Group.
- Week 2: Merge SDK defaults behind feature flag and ship a minor SDK release.
- Week 3: Enable runtime logging of headers in staging and run regression suite.
- Week 4: Run canary on 5% of requests for targeted routes, evaluate results.
- Week 5: Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if metrics are green.
Feature flags: client_resilience_v1 (boolean for SDKs), runtime_idempotency_logging (controls observability ingestion).
blockers: Need final sign-off from security on idempotency header format and confirmation that KMS/HSM logs will not leak envelope metadata. Also waiting on observability team to add two new spans for hedged-attempt and idempotency-collision events.
